# powerjp

> Japan power-grid data and observed-flow map.

powerjp is a reproducible open-data pipeline and static web map for exploring Japan's power-system topology, substations, generation facilities, and observed transmission-line power flow.

## Primary links

- Website: https://powerjp.mkhr.co.jp/
- Machine-readable description: https://powerjp.mkhr.co.jp/.well-known/ai.json
- Detailed project summary: https://powerjp.mkhr.co.jp/llms-full.txt
- Attribution and source terms: https://powerjp.mkhr.co.jp/ai.html

## Capabilities

- Map transmission-line and substation geometry.
- Inspect generation sites and unit-output layers.
- View observed trunk-line flow at 30-minute intervals.
- Inspect source attribution and published artifact metadata.

## Scope

- Geographic scope: Japan.
- Delivery: static GeoJSON and JSON artifacts through a CDN.
- Flow and unit-output resolution: 30 minutes where supplied by the source.
- Area supply-demand data: hourly upstream data used for derived estimates.

## Important distinction

powerjp visualizes observed flow. It is not an operational control system and does not claim that every displayed line is a newly calculated physical power-flow solution.

## Sources and licensing

Sources include All-Japan-Grid, OpenStreetMap, OCCTO public power-system data, MLIT National Land Numerical Information, and Global Energy Monitor. Code is MIT licensed. Data artifacts have source-specific conditions; ODbL applies to artifacts derived from All-Japan-Grid/OpenStreetMap. Read the in-application attribution before redistributing data.
